propositions.text: Applicant seeks to set aside a decision dated February 6, 2023 refusing her study permit application under section 216(1) IRPR.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, Ms. Hendabadi, seeks to set aside a decision dated February 6, 2023, by an officer (Officer) with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) refusing the Applicant’s application for a study permit pursuant to section 216(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR 2002/227 [IRPR] (the Decision).

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant seeks to set aside a February 6, 2023 decision refusing her study permit application under section 216(1) IRPR, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant asks Court to set aside Decision and send matter back for redetermination by a different officer due to unreasonableness and procedural unfairness
propositions.quote: The Applicant asks this Court to set the Decision aside and send the matter back for redetermination by a different officer because the decision is unreasonable and procedurally unfair.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant asks Court to set aside Decision and send matter back for redetermination due to unreasonableness and procedural unfairness.

propositions.text: Application is denied for the reasons that follow
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, this application is denied.

paragraphs.summary: Court denies the application for judicial review.

propositions.text: Applicant is a 33-year-old citizen of Iran
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a 33-year old citizen of Iran.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is a 33-year-old Iranian citizen.

propositions.text: Applicant has Bachelor and Master degrees in law-related fields and is self-employed as Legal Advisor and Legal and Financial Supervisor
propositions.quote: The Applicant has a Bachelor’s Degree in Law from the Islamic Azad University – South Tehran Branch and a Master’s Degree in Criminal Law and Criminology from the Islamic Azad University – Science and Research Tehran Branch. The Applicant is self-employed as a Legal Advisor and works as the Legal and Financial Supervisor at Kish Electronic Travel Company (eSafar).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant holds law degrees and works as Legal Advisor and Legal and Financial Supervisor.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicant's documentation did not show sufficient funds for studies in Canada
propositions.quote: The Decision indicates that the Officer found that the documentation provided in support of the Applicant’s application did not demonstrate that she had sufficient funds for the intended studies in Canada.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicant's study plan unreasonable given her employment and education history
propositions.quote: Further, the Officer found that the Applicant’s study plan was not reasonable in light of her employment and education history.

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant lacked sufficient funds and study plan was unreasonable given her background.

propositions.text: Officer reviewed application and considered financial documentation insufficient to prove funds availability
propositions.quote: I have reviewed the application. I have considered the following factors in my decision. Taking the applicant’s plan of studies into account, the documentation provided in support of the applicant’s financial situation does not demonstrate that the funds would be sufficient or available.

propositions.text: Bank statements lacked transactions showing history and availability of funds
propositions.quote: Bank statements provided did not include banking transactions to demonstrate the history of funds accumulation and the availability of these funds.

propositions.text: Absence of satisfactory documentation on source and availability of funds led to dissatisfaction about sufficiency of funds
propositions.quote: In the absence of satisfactory documentation showing the source and availability of these funds, I am not satisfied the applicant has sufficient funds for the intended studies in Canada.

propositions.text: Evidence of assets like vehicle, rental properties, or potential income was not included in available funds calculation
propositions.quote: Evidence of available funds associated with assets such as a vehicle, rental properties, or potential income, have not been included in the calculation of available funds.

propositions.text: Applicant's study plan was unreasonable given her prior studies and employment
propositions.quote: The applicant’s study plan does not appear reasonable given the applicant’s employment and education history: -The applicant has studies at the same academic level as the proposed studies in Canada and in an unrelated field.

propositions.text: Applicant has master's in criminal law and bachelor's in law, currently employed as legal advisor
propositions.quote: I note that the applicant obtained a master’s degree in criminal law and criminology and a bachelor’s degree of law. Applicant is currently employed as legal advisor.

propositions.text: Intended program shows inconsistent career progression given prior studies and career
propositions.quote: In light of the applicant’s previous studies and current career, the intended program of study appears to demonstrate an inconsistent career progression.

propositions.text: Employment letter does not mention need for international studies for employment or promotion
propositions.quote: I note that the applicant’s employment letter does not mention a need for international studies to secure employment or promotion.

propositions.text: Officer not satisfied Applicant will depart Canada at end of authorized stay
propositions.quote: Weighing the factors in this application, I am not satisfied that the applicant will depart Canada at the end of the period authorized for their stay.

propositions.text: Officer refused the application for these reasons
propositions.quote: For the reasons above, I have refused this application.

paragraphs.summary: Officer found financial evidence insufficient, study plan unreasonable, and was not satisfied Applicant would leave Canada; refused application.

propositions.text: Applicant commenced judicial review application on February 13, 2023; Court granted leave on March 21, 2024
propositions.quote: The Applicant commenced this application for leave and judicial review of the Decision on February 13, 2023. This Court granted leave for judicial review on March 21, 2024.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant started judicial review on Feb 13, 2023; Court granted leave on Mar 21, 2024.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer ignored or misunderstood evidence of financial means including accounts, prepaid tuition, financial aid, rental income, and family support
propositions.quote: The Applicant asserted that the Officer ignored or misunderstood evidence of her financial means to pay for the planned course of study in Canada. Specifically, the Applicant pointed to evidence of funds in her accounts, pre-paid tuition amounts, financial aid she will receive, and evidence of other assets including rental income from property in Iran and family support.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Decision was not reasonable given this financial evidence
propositions.quote: In view of this evidence, the Applicant argued that the Decision was not reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer ignored or misunderstood financial evidence and Decision was unreasonable.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer's finding on study plan utility was unreasonable due to inconsistency with prior studies and employment
propositions.quote: The Applicant asserted that the Officer’s finding on the utility of her planned course of study was not reasonable, as the Officer found that her previous studies and employment history were inconsistent with the plan of study to obtain an MBA.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer's finding on study plan utility was unreasonable due to inconsistency with prior background.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer ignored evidence of significant ties to Iran, making finding on departure unreasonable
propositions.quote: The Applicant asserted that the Officer ignored evidence of her significant ties to Iran, arguing that the finding that she will not depart Canada at the end of her studies was unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer ignored evidence of ties to Iran, making departure finding unreasonable.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer breached procedural fairness by not allowing response to concerns and failing to consider contradictory evidence
propositions.quote: Finally, the Applicant asserted that the Officer breached her right to procedural fairness by not providing her with an opportunity to respond to the concerns or deficiencies in her application. In addition, that the Officer failed to consider contradictory evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer breached procedural fairness by denying response opportunity and ignoring contradictory evidence.

propositions.text: Respondent argues Decision was reasonable; Officer entitled to review source, nature, and stability of financial means
propositions.quote: The Respondent argued that the Decision was reasonable. The Officer was entitled to review the source, nature, and stability of the Applicant’s financial means to engage in the proposed course of study.

propositions.text: Applicant bears burden to provide sufficient evidence; evidence did not meet section 220 IRPR requirements
propositions.quote: The Applicant has the burden to provide sufficient evidence to support their application. The evidence did not satisfy the requirements set out at section 220 of the IRPR.

propositions.text: Officer correctly denied the application
propositions.quote: Therefore, the Officer correctly denied the application.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Decision was reasonable; Applicant failed to meet evidence burden; Officer correctly denied application.

propositions.text: Respondent argues Officer's reasons entitled to deference; Applicant gave general assertions without specific benefits of program
propositions.quote: The Respondent argued that the Officer’s reasons were entitled to deference. Here the application does not sufficiently highlight why the proposed plan of study was required. Rather, the Applicant sets out some general assertions, but no specific information concerning the benefits of the proposed program.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Officer's reasons deserve deference; Applicant gave general assertions without specifics on program benefits.

propositions.text: Issues: Was Officer's refusal unreasonable? Did Officer breach procedural fairness?
propositions.quote: This application raises the following two issues: Was the Officer’s decision to deny the Applicant’s study permit unreasonable? Did the Officer breach the Applicant’s right to procedural fairness in their review of the study permit application?

paragraphs.summary: Court identifies issues: unreasonableness of refusal and breach of procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Standard of review for visa officer's refusal of study permit is reasonableness, per Vavilov
propositions.quote: The parties submitted, and I agree, that that standard of review applicable to a visa officer’s refusal of a study permit is reasonableness (Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov] at paras 10, 23).

paragraphs.summary: Court states standard of review is reasonableness per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Reasonableness review is deferential, requiring decision to be transparent, intelligible, justified
propositions.quote: Reasonableness review is a deferential standard, and requires an evaluation of the administrative decision to determine if the decision is transparent, intelligible, and justified (Vavilov at paras 12–15, and 95).

propositions.text: Reasonableness means decision is internally coherent, rational, and justified in relation to facts and law
propositions.quote: Pursuant to the Vavilov framework, a reasonable decision is “one that is based on an internally coherent and rational chain of analysis and that is justified in relation to the facts and law” (Vavilov at para 85).

paragraphs.summary: Court explains reasonableness review is deferential and requires coherent, justified decision per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Court may intervene only if error is central or significant and renders decision unreasonable
propositions.quote: To intervene on an application for judicial review, the Court must find an error in the decision that is central or significant, which renders the decision unreasonable (Vavilov at para 100).

paragraphs.summary: Court may intervene only if error is central or significant and makes decision unreasonable.

propositions.text: Officers need not respond to every argument but must meaningfully grapple with key issues
propositions.quote: Officers are not required to respond to every argument or piece of evidence advanced in an application or make an explicit finding on each element; however, the reasons must demonstrate that the officer “meaningfully grapple[d]” with key issues or central arguments raised (Vavilov at para 128).

propositions.text: Officers under pressure cannot provide extensive reasons; brief decisions are reasonable if responsive to evidence
propositions.quote: This Court has noted that due to the significant pressure on visa officers to review a large volume of applications on a daily basis, officers are not able to provide “extensive reasons” for every matter (Patel v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2020 FC 77 [Patel]). Accordingly, this Court has found that brief decisions are reasonable if they are responsive to the evidence (Patel at para 15).

propositions.text: Concise and simple reasons are acceptable if responsive to evidence
propositions.quote: In other words, an officer’s reasons “may be concise and simple so long they are responsive to the evidence” (Ibekwe v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2022 FC 728 at para 28, citing Patel at para 17).

paragraphs.summary: Court explains officers need not address every argument but must meaningfully grapple; brief, responsive reasons suffice.

propositions.text: Applicant must establish satisfaction of Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and IRPR requirements
propositions.quote: An applicant for a study permit must establish that they satisfy the requirements of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 and the IRPR.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant must satisfy Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and IRPR requirements.

propositions.text: Section 216 of the IRPR requires an officer to issue a study permit if certain criteria are met after examination.
propositions.quote: Section 216 of the IRPR sets out that an officer shall issue a study permit to a foreign national if, following an examination, certain criteria are satisfied.

propositions.text: The onus is on the applicant to satisfy the officer they will not remain in Canada after visa expiry.
propositions.quote: The onus is on the applicant to satisfy the officer that they will not remain in Canada following the expiration of their visa

propositions.text: Solopova and Nourani cases confirm the applicant's onus to prove non-remainance after visa expiry.
propositions.quote: (Solopova v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 690 at para 10; Nourani v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2023 FC 732 at para 14)

paragraphs.summary: The court states section 216 IRPR requires an officer to issue a study permit if criteria are met; applicant must prove they won't remain after visa expiry, citing Solopova and Nourani.

propositions.text: Section 220 IRPR requires proof of sufficient financial resources without working in Canada to cover tuition, maintenance, and transport costs.
propositions.quote: Section 220 of the IRPR provides that an officer shall not issue a study permit unless it is established that the applicant has sufficient and available financial resources, without working in Canada, to: pay tuition and fees; maintain themselves and accompanying family members; and pay the costs of transport for themselves and accompanying family members to and from Canada

propositions.text: Ohuaregbe and Adekoya cases confirm financial resource requirements under section 220 IRPR.
propositions.quote: (Ohuaregbe v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2023 FC 480 at para 23 [Ohuaregbe] citing Adekoya v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 1234 at para 9)

paragraphs.summary: The court explains section 220 IRPR requires proof of sufficient financial resources without working in Canada, citing Ohuaregbe and Adekoya.

propositions.text: Officers may require proof of funds for the entire academic program and must be satisfied about source, nature, stability, and future income likelihood.
propositions.quote: Officers may require proof of sufficient funds for the entirety of an academic program, and pursuant to the IRPR they “must be satisfied as to the source, nature and stability of those funds, as well as to determine the likelihood of future income and the ability to pay for subsequent years of education and living expenses”

propositions.text: Sani and Sayyar cases support the detailed financial investigation required under IRPR.
propositions.quote: (Sani v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2024 FC 396 at paras 13–32. See also Sayyar v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2023 FC 494 at para 12 [Sayyar])

paragraphs.summary: The court states officers may require proof of funds for entire program and must be satisfied about source, nature, stability, and future income, citing Sani and Sayyar.

propositions.text: If an applicant does not meet section 220 IRPR financial requirements, the officer must deny the study permit application without discretion.
propositions.quote: Where an applicant does not meet the requirements set out in section 220 of the IRPR, the officer has no discretion and must deny the application for a study permit

propositions.text: Ohuaregbe confirms the officer's lack of discretion if financial requirements are unmet.
propositions.quote: (Ohuaregbe at para 23)

paragraphs.summary: The court states officers must deny study permits if financial requirements under section 220 IRPR are unmet, citing Ohuaregbe.

propositions.text: Officers may consider financial means beyond the first year of studies and must investigate nature, source, and stability of funds.
propositions.quote: visa officers “should be satisfied however that the probability of funding for future years does exist.” In other words, officers may consider financial means beyond the first year of planned studies. An officer’s investigation into an applicant’s financial means is a detailed and complete investigation into the nature, source, and stability of the funds

propositions.text: Sayyar case clarifies the detailed financial investigation required under section 220 IRPR.
propositions.quote: (Sayyar at para 12)

paragraphs.summary: The court explains officers may consider funding beyond first year and must investigate fund nature, source, and stability, citing Sayyar.

propositions.text: The Officer found the Applicant's documentation did not demonstrate sufficient or available funds and lacked satisfactory proof of source and availability.
propositions.quote: the Officer found that the documentation provided in support of the Applicant’s application “does not demonstrate that the funds would be sufficient or available,” and that the application does not include “satisfactory documentation showing the source and availability of these funds.”

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Applicant's documentation insufficient to prove funds' sufficiency, availability, and source.

propositions.text: The onus is on the applicant to provide sufficient information; visa officers are not required to investigate further or allow clarifications.
propositions.quote: The onus is on an applicant to ensure that there is sufficient information before the visa officer to assess their application. Visa officers are not required to further investigate or provide an opportunity for applicants to clarify their application or provide additional information to supplement their application

propositions.text: Ohuaregbe confirms visa officers' lack of duty to investigate or allow clarifications.
propositions.quote: (Ohuaregbe at paras 31–33)

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicant must provide sufficient information; visa officers need not investigate or allow clarifications, citing Ohuaregbe.

propositions.text: The Decision is reasonable; the Officer found the Applicant failed to meet section 220 IRPR financial requirements.
propositions.quote: The Decision is reasonable. The Officer considered the evidence set out in the application and found that the Applicant failed to satisfy the requirements set out at section 220 of the IRPR, namely to demonstrate sufficient funds to pay for the planned course of study in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Decision reasonable as the Officer found the Applicant failed to meet financial requirements under section 220 IRPR.

propositions.text: The financial issue alone disposes of the judicial review; the Officer had no discretion to grant the permit without financial satisfaction.
propositions.quote: This issue alone is dispositive of the application for judicial review. The Officer, having found that the evidence did not satisfy the financial requirements under section 220 of the IRPR, did not have discretion to grant the study permit.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the financial issue alone disposes of the judicial review; the Officer lacked discretion to grant the permit without financial satisfaction.

propositions.text: The Applicant asserted multiple breaches of procedural fairness in her Memorandum of Argument.
propositions.quote: The Applicant asserted a number of breaches of procedural fairness in her Memorandum of Argument.

propositions.text: The Court has recently considered and rejected these procedural fairness arguments in multiple cases.
propositions.quote: This Court has considered these arguments recently in a number of other matters. In Amirhesari v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2024 FC 436, Justice Ahmed noted: ... I have rejected them ... My colleagues have routinely rejected them ...

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant alleged procedural fairness breaches; the court finds these arguments have been recently considered and rejected in multiple cases.

propositions.text: The procedural fairness arguments were not pursued at oral argument and are without merit.
propositions.quote: These arguments were not relied upon in oral argument. ... These arguments are without merit.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the procedural fairness arguments were not pursued orally and are without merit.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is denied.
propositions.quote: In light of the foregoing, this application for judicial review is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The court denies the application for judicial review.

propositions.text: No question is certified; the application for judicial review is denied.
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review is denied. No question is certified.

propositions.text: The judgment is issued by Judge Julie Blackhawk of the Federal Court on June 25, 2024, with appearances and solicitors noted.
propositions.quote: “Julie Blackhawk” Judge FEDERAL COURT ... DATED: JUNE 25, 2024 ... APPEARANCES: Oluwadamilola Asuni For The Applicant Justin Zelowski For The Respondent ... SOLICITORS OF RECORD: Oluwadamilola Asuni Barrister and Solicitor Saskatoon, Saskatchewan For The Applicant Attorney General of Canada Saskatoon, Saskatchewan For The Respondent

paragraphs.summary: The court denies the review, certifies no question, and issues judgment with appearances and solicitors noted.
